body: Sunday, July 05 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed held rates steady at new Chair Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting, and Warsh declined to signal a July direction at the ECB Sintra forum. The 2Y yield at 4.14% (prior close, +6 bps vs 4W) is repricing hawkishly even as the 10Y at 4.49% (unchanged vs 4W) stays flat — the curve spread at +35 bps remains positive but still flat, 6 bps narrower than four weeks ago, with the narrowing pressure coming from the front end. Fiscal policy remains expansionary with the administration touting the stock market rally and tax cuts.

New / Most Important: June payrolls shocked to the downside at just 57,000 jobs added, sending the dollar tumbling and gold surging on the day. This is the most important data point of the week — it opens the door for easing later this year but Warsh's deliberate opacity means the market cannot front-run a cut. The juxtaposition of a weak labor print against "rate hike readjustment" headlines in Yahoo Finance suggests the market is genuinely confused about the reaction function under new Fed leadership. This is structurally new: Warsh's communication style is a hard break from the Powell/Bernanke era of forward guidance. He is deliberately withholding signal, which forces the market to become more data-dependent and raises vol around each print. Expect this regime to structurally re-price rate volatility (MOVE index) higher over time, as the Fed put's strike price becomes unknowable. For portfolio construction, this means carry trades and duration bets need wider stops and smaller sizing than under the prior regime.

Playbook ✓: Supreme Court ruling affirming Fed independence was a positive — consensus expected this would be benign for markets, and it was. The Nasdaq underperforming (↓4.1% vs 4W) while Russell outperforms (↑3.5%) is the classic late-cycle rotation script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The 57K payrolls print is a potential inflection — if this is the start of a labor market rollover, it contradicts the "soaring Trump economy" narrative. Consumer confidence at historic lows while equity markets rally is a classic late-cycle divergence. The FT's "good vibes masking a reset" and "surging profit forecasts fueling fears of an earnings bubble" headlines confirm institutional unease beneath the surface.

Macro Stance: Eurozone inflation fell more than expected to 2.8% in June as the energy shock continues to fade. Lagarde stated the ECB does not need to fight inflation with "the same force" as in 2022-23 and cited Europe's economic resilience as giving greater room to maneuver on rates.

New / Most Important: The below-consensus inflation print is the key development — it materially strengthens the case for the ECB to hold or cut at its next decision. The euro slipped on the print as rate expectations repriced dovishly. Sterling gained ground against a weakening dollar, reflecting relative UK resilience.

Playbook ✓: Disinflation continuing on the back of energy base effects is textbook and consensus. European bonds rallying in Q3 is the expected playbook per Morningstar's outlook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Lagarde's tone at Sintra was notably more confident on growth resilience than expected — this creates a tension between cutting for inflation reasons and holding for growth reasons. If the ECB opts to hold despite sub-3% inflation, it would be a hawkish surprise relative to the market's dovish lean.

Macro Stance: The PBOC is easing funding while refusing to chase the bond rally. Overnight reverse repos debuted at 1.25% (Reuters, [Jun 28]) and the injection was doubled (Reuters, [Jun 29]); it then signalled easing with a trillion-yuan outright reverse repo, ending a three-month tapering streak (BigGo Finance, [Jul 3]), while cutting bond purchases on wariness over falling yields (Bloomberg, [Jul 2]), so net bond operations injected only 10 billion yuan in June (Macau Business, [Jul 3]). Liquidity now comes through repo, not outright bond buying. The fix leans against weakness: USD/CNY was set at 6.8047 against 6.8088 (TMGM, [Jul 3]), firmer than estimates, which VT Markets reads as managed strength amid softer growth [Jul 3], and HSBC says structural forces still support the RMB (Exchange Rates UK, [Jul 4]). May CPI rose only 1.2% (China Daily, [Jun 10]) while factory-gate inflation hit a near four-year high (Reuters, [Jun 9]); Caixin warns deflation risks are squeezing profits [Jun 30].

PMIs & Activity: June's upturn is narrow. The official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 and non-manufacturing to 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]); the private factory gauge grew for a seventh month (China Daily, [Jul 2]) but less than expected (Bloomberg, [Jun 30]). Services slowed slightly (Reuters, [Jul 2]), though by less than forecast (The Business Times, [Jul 3]). Consumption is rolling over: NEV retail sales fell 7% in June (CnEVPost, [Jul 3]) as the subsidy pullback hits auto and appliance sales (Nikkei Asia, [Jul 2]). May's split stands: industrial output growth quickened while retail sales and investment contracted (Reuters, [Jun 15]); exports jumped 19.4% (AP News, [Jun 9]), but retail sales fell 0.6% (Il Sole 24 Ore, [Jun 15]), fixed-asset investment fell 4.1% in five months (Macau Business, [Jun 16]) and profit growth slowed for the first time in six months (Times of India, [Jun 27]).

Credit Impulse: Total social financing grew 7.7% in May (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]), but new loans missed as the property slump curbed demand (Reuters, [Jun 12]): government bonds, not private demand. Stress is visible at the edges: China took over private lender Zhongbang Bank, citing credit risks (The Standard, [Jul 3]); Beijing is capping LGFV bond yields (IFR, [Jul 2]); and Le Monde describes Guizhou's bridge and highway boom running up against a wall of debt [Jul 4]. With debt above 300% of GDP (UPI, [Jun 29]), the private impulse is negative and the local-government channel is spent.

Property: Asia Times says the housing market is in free fall as buyers wait for floor prices [Jul 3], and Briefs Finance has home prices slipping again [Jul 3], consistent with resale prices falling faster in June (Reuters, [Jun 30]). Sales are concentrating, not recovering: top-tier cities overtook regional hubs (Caixin, [Jul 3]), and the top 100 developers' June sales rose 11.8% month on month on a half-year push (Moomoo, [Jul 1]). Real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]). Resolution is state-led: Vanke named a former Shenzhen financial regulator as president (Caixin, [Jul 3]) and Country Garden cleared its first offshore coupon (Caixin, [Jul 2]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal support is receding: vehicle and vessel tax breaks for NEVs and energy-saving cars are ending (China Daily HK, [Jul 4]) and a tax crackdown is hitting listed firms (SCMP, [Jul 2]). Control is rising, with curbs on foreign investments (Times of India, [Jul 1]) and a landmark law over offshore tech transfers (SCMP, [Jul 1]). On trade, Beijing signals openness to cut the EU deficit as Brussels toughens (SCMP, [Jul 3]); von der Leyen says the EU will retaliate if China misses October (Euronews, [Jul 3]), while the chief trade MEP calls that deadline "not realistic at all" (Euronews, [Jul 3]). The state iron ore buyer extended restrictions on Fortescue (Bloomberg, [Jul 3]), and China and the US target tariff cuts on farm goods (Bloomberg, [Jul 2]).

Markets & Flows: China shares ended higher as technology stocks rebounded (Business Standard, [Jul 3]) and the Hang Seng rose 0.8% on tech and financials (Dimsum Daily, [Jul 3]), after a three-week mainland low (The Star, [Jul 2]). Wall Street banks are recovering in China amid a trading boom (FT, [Jul 4]), and mainland investors are buying Hong Kong shares, favouring SMIC and Zhipu AI (SCMP, [Jul 3]): the flow is into AI and brokers, not the domestic cycle. The capital wall keeps rising, with curbs on higher-yielding offshore debt (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]) and a shutdown of retail gold trading (TipRanks, [Jul 1]).

New / Most Important: The newest China signal is geopolitical: Iran's envoy says Beijing will get Hormuz concessions (Bloomberg, [Jul 4]). For an importer with weak domestic demand, secured and cheaper crude is a terms-of-trade gift and helps explain why the PBOC can lean on the fix. It does nothing for the domestic problem that Guizhou illustrates: the local governments that built the last cycle cannot fund the next one, and households are not borrowing to replace them.

Playbook ✓: Continued easing at the front end, falling home prices, receding subsidies and a managed yuan are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The oil collapse is not a China-demand signal on its own; it is supply (the Strait of Hormuz reopening, Beijing's concessions, some fuel export curbs lifted on ample supplies per Bloomberg [Jun 30]) meeting a Chinese economy whose PMI strength is all exports. Transmission runs three ways. Bulk commodities: the state iron ore buyer's extended Fortescue restrictions and real-estate investment down 16.2% hit iron ore and the AUD directly. Europe: the WSJ says China is devastating the last stronghold of German industry [Jul 3], a share loss that hurts European exporters whether or not October brings retaliation. EM: cheaper crude flatters importers, while excess Chinese supply exports disinflation through goods prices even with a firmer fix. Hong Kong rallies on AI and broker flows are flows, not fundamentals.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is under intensifying pressure to hike as the yen continues to weaken and the economy remains robust. Japan spent $74 billion on yen intervention, yet yen weakness persists as markets see the BOJ falling behind the curve. The BOJ has also shed 15.6% of its massive balance sheet via QT.

New / Most Important: This is the most structurally significant story in global macro right now. The BOJ's "monetary monster is turning on its maker" as Asia Times put it — and a government panel member explicitly called for moderate rate hikes. The BOJ is simultaneously running QT and being pushed toward its first rate hike cycle in decades, which creates a dual tightening impulse with global ramifications. The yen carry trade unwind risk is live: if the BOJ hikes, the estimated $1T+ in yen-funded carry positions globally would need to partially reverse, sending shockwaves through EM assets, US Treasuries, and European credit. The fact that Japan's economy is robust enough to absorb tightening removes the last excuse for inaction. Wolf Street's documentation of the 15.6% balance sheet reduction shows this is already happening via QT — the rate hike would be the second shoe to drop. Cross-border capital flow implications are enormous: Japanese institutional money has been the single largest private buyer of foreign bonds for years, and a higher domestic rate would pull that flow home.

Playbook ✓: Yen weakness forcing intervention is well-known and expected.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The BOJ's "slow, dovish revamp" casting doubt on long-term hike plans (Reuters) is directly at odds with the market pricing of an imminent hike — one side is wrong, and the magnitude of the mismatch is widening.

Macro Stance: The RBA minutes confirmed a unanimous hold with inflation risk still live. The RBA warned that union inflation expectations are too high, and stated policy needs to remain restrictive. The AUD weakened despite hawkish minutes, reflecting broader USD dynamics and commodity weakness.

New / Most Important: An RBA briefing suggesting near-zero interest rates are "closer than you think" is a fascinating dovish outlier from the institution's own research arm, even as the operational stance remains hawkish.  |  Playbook ✓: The "waiting game" posture is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: China's construction slump and oil's 26% crash are devastating for Australia's terms of trade — China's real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May and its state iron ore buyer extended restrictions on Fortescue. The hawkish RBA stance is increasingly at odds with a collapsing commodity complex — if the terms of trade deterioration accelerates, the RBA will be forced to pivot faster than its current rhetoric suggests.

Macro Stance: The NBP is in a holding pattern the data justify from both sides. June CPI printed 2.5% per the GUS flash, at target and below forecasts (Parkiet, [Jun 30]), with GUS crediting fruit, vegetables and cheap imports (Bankier.pl, [Jul 2]). Commerzbank noted that rate hike bets have vanished, while ING sees the market starting to play for cuts in the second half of 2026 [Jun 30]. Ahead of the RPP's July meeting, CEO Magazyn expects rates most likely unchanged [Jul 2]. The reason not to front-run a cut is fuel: Gazeta Prawna warned that the end of the CPN package could lift inflation toward 3% [Jun 30], and INFOR.PL flagged a double monthly hit to electricity bills [Jul 5]. The reason to keep a cut on the table is activity: the manufacturing PMI dropped to 46.1 in June against a 49.4 consensus (Do Rzeczy, [Jul 1]). Wages remain sticky: construction is paying up to 36 thousand zł to find workers (Money.pl, [Jul 2]) and unions called the 2027 minimum wage proposal a "mockery" (Dziennik.pl, [Jul 4]).

Markets: Warsaw enters the week at records. The WIG20 added 7.38% in the second quarter, its third consecutive positive quarter (FXMAG, [Jul 1]), Żabka, XTB and GPW itself set all-time highs (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 2]), and Friday's session delivered a 1.57% index gain with 19 of 20 members up (FXMAG, [Jul 3]). The card's weekly scoreboard: Orlen 132.92 (+7.7% 1W, -7.0% 4W) after a 4.78% jump on a record net profit (Investing.com Polska, [Jul 3]); CD Projekt 233.4 (+7.4% 1W) on Cyberpunk 2077 passing 40 mn copies (PAP Biznes, [Jul 3]) and its best Steam interest since 2023 (PPE, [Jul 5]); Allegro 38.44 (+3.3% 1W, +9.5% 4W); KGHM 335.0 (+2.2% 1W, -3.0% 4W); Pekao 233.2 (+1.9% 1W); PKO 105.24 (+1.6% 1W, +7.1% 4W); LPP 18,550 (+1.3% 1W, -14.1% 4W); PGE 9.63 (+0.3% 1W, -6.1% 4W). Dino is the lone loser at 27.7 (-4.4% 1W, -6.3% 4W), its lowest since 2022 after Barclays cut its target on slower expansion (pb.pl, [Jul 3]). EPOL's last close was 39.44 (+2.3% 1W, -1.3% 4W). The zloty is the weak link: EUR/PLN tested 4.30 on the inflation surprise (wnp.pl, [Jul 1]) before a soft US payrolls print sank the dollar and let the zloty recover (Comparic.pl, [Jul 3]); the card shows USD/PLN 3.7522 (-0.4% 1W, +2.9% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.2859 (+0.2% 1W, +1.2% 4W). Inwestycje.pl argued the high budget deficit could weigh on the zloty in the second half [Jul 3]. POLGBs have support: investors returned to Polish debt and bought bonds worth billions in May (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 3]).

Fiscal & Politics: The fuel shield is the live fiscal fight. The CPN package has ended with pump prices up around 60 groszy per litre (wPolityce.pl, [Jul 1]), the government intends to recoup the 4 bn zł cost through a windfall tax on fuel companies (Biznes Wprost, [Jul 2]), and PiS has tabled a bill to cut VAT and excise on fuel for the holiday season (RadioMaryja.pl, [Jul 2]). The Sejm passed the OKI personal investment account with up to 100 thousand zł sheltered from the Belka tax (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 3]). The sovereign picture is the overhang: the EU convergence report ranked Poland's public finances the worst in the bloc (wPolityce.pl, [Jun 30]), and Do Rzeczy carried a warning that Poland could go the way of Greece [Jul 3]. The finance minister admitted there is "no chemistry" with the president (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 2]).

Corporate & Sectors: Banks have a date for the end of WIBOR: the finance ministry confirmed when the benchmark disappears for borrowers (Bankier.pl, [Jul 5]), which Money.pl called a seismic change for Poles with loans [Jul 5]. That follows the TSUE ruling of Jul 2 preserving lenders' right to recover disbursed capital on void CHF loans, which Rzeczpospolita said had banks opening champagne [Jul 2]. Energy policy was reset over the weekend: Tusk declared the end of coal and named Bełchatów and Konin as good locations for the second nuclear plant (Bankier.pl, [Jul 4]), with Bankier.pl's follow-up arguing coal guarantees security today and nuclear must secure it tomorrow [Jul 5]; Orlen switched on a farm supplying 100 thousand homes (Money.pl, [Jul 4]). KGHM's Strategy 2055+ carries over 32 bn zł of investment to 2030 (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 3]) and a polyhalite mine near Puck on a 300 mn tonne deposit (Money.pl, [Jul 3]), though the company is in mourning after a fatal accident at the Głogów smelter (wnp.pl, [Jul 5]). Dino added nearly 150 stores in the half (Omnichannel News, [Jul 3]) yet faces OPZZ strike threats (Biznes Wprost, [Jul 3]), and housing prices beat inflation again (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Jul 5]).

Geopolitics & Security: The US warning that Russia is discussing an armed provocation on Polish territory to test NATO (The Telegraph, [Jul 3]) is being digested: Politico reported from the eastern flank [Jul 5], EUobserver argued an attack on Poland would be Putin's last failure [Jul 5], and The Baltic Sentinel called Poland's warnings alarming but unclear [Jul 5]. Tusk said the coming months may be "critical" (BBC, [Jul 3]) and told Bloomberg Poland should be cautious in pledging aid for Ukraine [Jul 3], while The Telegraph wrote that Zelensky has a Poland problem [Jul 5]. MON will declassify all donations to Ukraine from 2022 to 2026 (Strefa Obrony, [Jul 5]).

New / Most Important: No material change: lower inflation makes a future cut more likely but timing remains unclear, and the weekend's substance was policy rather than data. The WIBOR end-date and the CHF ruling together remove two legal overhangs from the bank sector in one week, which matters more for PKO and Pekao than the rate path, and Tusk's coal exit with a two-site nuclear shortlist is a decade-long capex commitment landing on a budget the EU already rates worst in the bloc. The zloty, not equities, is where that fiscal story will be priced.  |  Playbook ✓: PLN capped by dovish repricing is consensus; banks benefit from legal clarity regardless of the RPP.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Fuel and power bills rising into a 2.5% print mean headline CPI has likely troughed; a market playing for cuts while energy costs re-accelerate is the mismatch to watch.

Macro Stance: The Indian rupee slipped to a two-week low as US Treasury yields surged, and sustained capital outflows continued with foreign stock buy-sell activity up 25%. Fair Observer's piece framing India's "reckoning — reform or regression?" captures the structural debate.

New / Most Important: Capital outflow acceleration is the key signal. The 25% rise in foreign buy-sell activity amid net outflows suggests institutional rebalancing away from India.  |  Playbook ✓: EM FX weakness on higher US rates is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: India is seeing outflows even as the dollar weakened post-payrolls, suggesting India-specific factors (valuations, reform stall) rather than pure dollar dynamics.

Narrative: Bearish: the Nasdaq 100 at 29,329 is down 4.1% vs 4W, the sharpest underperformance in the snapshot, as hyperscaler capex is called "insane" and AI-bubble fears go mainstream. Microsoft at a 52-week low is the emblem of the rotation, while Zoom buying AI platform Common Room shows second-tier software buying AI rather than building it.

Reported: Progress Software is skyrocketing (The Motley Fool, [Jul 1]) after Q2 profit rose 24% (SaasRise, [Jul 1]). Concentrix plunged 25% after a Q2 earnings miss and weak guidance (ChartMill, [Jun 29]).
EPS Upside Watch: Salesforce — up 5.5% after beating Q1 targets and raising its revenue outlook (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 29]). BILL Holdings — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 2]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Microsoft at a 52-week low while the S&P 500 sits within 1% of recent highs is a regime break: the K-shape is running through tech itself, AI hardware winners against cloud and software losers. The "Mag 7 as safe haven" thesis is dead for now.

Narrative: Mixed: XLC is dragged by the mega-cap de-rating but less than pure tech, given its media and telecom mix; Starlink's potential IPO path keeps SpaceX the highest-optionality story in communications.
Reported: Prosus' profit got a boost from food delivery, travel bookings and Tencent (Business Day, [Jun 29]).
EPS Upside Watch: SoftBank — Citi raised its target on profit growth (Yahoo Finance Australia, [Jun 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Legacy media value is being unlocked by break-ups rather than growth: Comcast plans to separate its media and technology businesses into two public companies (Comcast Corporation, [Jun 29]). Splits, not ad cycles, may drive the next re-rating in old media.

Narrative: Bullish: financials gain from the rotation into value and small caps (Russell ↑3.5%), though a curve at +35 bps is still too flat to do much for NIM; Arch Capital's new CEOs and Northern Trust's fund-admin wins show healthy organic growth.

Reported: CMC Markets lifted guidance for FY net operating income and the shares surged (Sharecast.com, [Jul 1]). FactSet's Q3 earnings beat estimates on organic revenue growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 1]).

EPS Upside Watch: ICICI, SBI and HDFC Bank — set to gain as lending yields stabilise on slow deposit repricing (Economic Times, [Jul 4]). Bank of America — its dividend is still too small for its earnings (TIKR.com, [Jul 4]), room for higher payouts.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Robinhood appearing in a Dow futures preview suggests it has graduated from meme stock to institutional consideration — retail brokerage is now part of the mainstream financials trade, not a side bet.

Narrative: Bearish: WTI at 68.78 has cratered 26.1% in 4 weeks as the Strait of Hormuz reopening removed the geopolitical premium. The demand read is ambiguous: China's official PMI is still at 50.3, but its NEV retail sales fell 7% in June and its services gauge slipped.
Reported: Energy Transfer raised its 2026 guidance by $750 million (TIKR.com, [Jun 29]). Nigeria's NNPC said its profit fell despite higher oil production in May (Premium Times Nigeria, [Jul 2]).

EPS Upside Watch: US oil companies — see a big profit jump as they gird for a clash with Trump over pump prices (Reuters, [Jul 3]). Patterson-UTI Energy — analysts lifted fair value as they raise earnings views (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 3]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: A 26% oil fall with the VIX at only 16.15 is historically anomalous; in the 2014 and 2020 crashes equity volatility spiked. Either this is a benign supply shock, or the market is complacent about high-yield energy credit, EM petrostates and capex cancellations.
Narrative: Bullish: industrials benefit from the small-cap rotation and the domestic manufacturing theme, and Honeywell's post-spin structure gives a cleaner automation thesis.

Reported: AeroVironment's Q4 earnings beat sent the stock soaring (Quartz, [Jul 3]). MSC Industrial beat analyst estimates (Simply Wall Street, [Jul 4]) on price gains and volume growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 2]). Maersk sharply raised 2026 guidance on stronger-than-expected container demand (iMarine, [Jul 2]).
EPS Upside Watch: Delta and United — BofA sees them entering a rare airline sweet spot (TheStreet, [Jul 4]), with Delta's Q2 report next (The Globe and Mail, [Jul 3]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The airline bull case is narrowly American: IATA expects airline profits to halve in 2026 (The Edge Malaysia, [Jul 1]) even as BofA calls a sweet spot for US carriers. Domestic pricing, not cheap fuel alone, has to carry it.

Narrative: Mixed: consumer confidence at historic lows against rallying equities is the central tension, and the 57K payrolls print adds labour anxiety; lower oil helps, but the jobs miss matters more for discretionary spending.

Reported: Nike posted a Q4 earnings beat, but tariff refunds mask its China struggles (Quartz, [Jul 3]). Tesla's deliveries beat forecasts as Europe's rebound brightened the outlook (Fox Business, [Jul 2]). Rivian raised its 2026 delivery outlook while Lucid missed expectations (CNBC, [Jul 2]).

EPS Upside Watch: Sodexo — raised its full-year organic revenue growth forecast on a strong quarter (Reuters, [Jul 2]). Restaurant Brands — Burger King's turnaround is putting it back in focus (MarketBeat, [Jul 1]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Good news is being sold: Tesla's stock sank to its worst day in a year despite blowout delivery numbers (MarketWatch, [Jul 2]). With confidence at historic lows, positioning rather than data is setting prices.
Narrative: Bullish: staples are the defensive rotation beneficiary as tech sells off and the labour market weakens, and lower energy costs are a direct margin tailwind.

Reported: General Mills posted a Q4 beat and targets $3B in cost savings (Quartz, [Jul 3]). Constellation Brands' Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue fell 3.3% (Quartz, [Jul 3]). National Beverage released Q4 earnings and the stock rose (Quiver Quantitative, [Jul 1]).

EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola — its fourth consecutive earnings beat sets up a run toward a new high (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 3]). Berjaya Food — the Paris Baguette disposal clears an earnings drag (NST Online, [Jul 2]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The staples rally runs on cost cuts, not volume: General Mills' organic sales were flat y/y (TradingView, [Jul 1]) and Constellation's revenue fell. If savings, not demand, carry earnings, the defensive premium is thinner than it looks.
Narrative: Bullish: healthcare's defensive profile suits the rotation, and Biogen flagged as undervalued shows large-cap biotech acting as the late-cycle haven.

Reported: Craneware's shares slumped after slower conversion triggered a profit warning (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 3]). Piramal Pharma's FY2026 annual report showed a net loss amid destocking and exceptional items (scanx.trade, [Jul 3]).

EPS Upside Watch: Eli Lilly — the case for double-digit upside (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 1]) rests on revenue that surged 56% (BigGo Finance, [Jul 4]). UnitedHealth — Morgan Stanley raised its price target ahead of Q2 earnings (TIKR.com, [Jul 1]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Not everyone is chasing GLP-1: J&J is betting on diversification over the hype (BigGo Finance, [Jul 4]), a reminder that one drug class now drives much of the sector's earnings growth — and its concentration risk.

Narrative: Bearish: copper at 6.22 (↓4.4%) trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal, so its dip tracks AI sentiment. The China read comes from property: real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May and home prices slipped again in June.
Reported: No major reports this week; Fortescue, downgraded, contemplates a future without growth (The Australian, [Jul 3]).

EPS Upside Watch: Nickel Industries — its price target was raised and the analyst remains bullish (TheBull.com.au, [Jul 2]). PetChem — Petronas' buyout of the PPC stake is seen lifting its earnings (NST Online, [Jun 30]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Chinese chemical makers are guiding up while the tape stays Bearish: mid-year earnings forecasts are out, with the highest projected growth at 952% and several positive preliminary results (Moomoo, [Jul 4]).
Narrative: Mixed: a 10Y at 4.49%, unchanged vs 4W, is still a headwind, wealthy investors say they are done being landlords, and affordability stress in Australia shows the problem is global.
Reported: Tosei REIT's distribution hit a record ¥3,926 for a fourth straight term (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 29]).

EPS Upside Watch: D.R. Horton — is defying the housing gloom (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 4]). Supermarket Income REIT — completed a £445 million refinancing to cut borrowing costs (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jul 2]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The market's verdict on retail REITs may be wrong: Realty Income yields 5% because investors agreed retail REITs are toxic (24/7 Wall St., [Jul 2]), yet it still has room to raise its dividend through 2030 (TIKR.com, [Jul 2]).

Narrative: Bullish: utilities have a dual tailwind from the defensive rotation and AI power demand, lower oil cuts input costs for gas-fired generation, and Deloitte's 2026-2031 forecast ties AI investment to energy demand.
Reported: No major reports this week.

EPS Upside Watch: WEC Energy — data centres make its growth story more attractive (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 1]). NextEra Energy — partnerships and PPAs are the question for its earnings growth (TradingView, [Jul 2]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consolidation is the new risk: NextEra's bid to create the world's largest utility raises serious concerns (Center for American Progress, [Jul 1]), so regulators, not demand, may cap the AI-power trade.
Narrative: Bearish: there are few direct signals; lower oil is marginally positive for combustion-engine demand but does not offset EV-transition costs and weak Chinese demand.

Reported: Mercedes cut R&D jobs as German luxury car sales in China halved (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 29]). Supplier KPIT Technologies slid 16% on weak Q1 guidance as European automakers cut spending (The Financial Express, [Jul 1]).
EPS Upside Watch: Volkswagen — considers 100,000 job cuts and plant closures (Business Chief, [Jul 1]), a cost lever for margins.

⚡ Breaking Convention: China's carmakers once prized domestic sales — now they export or suffer, and Volkswagen shows why (Automotive News, [Jul 2]). That export push lands in Europe, moving the China problem onto European home turf.

Narrative: Mixed: the feed is full of AI hardware stories — Nvidia's Blackwell demand turning into usage-linked revenue, AMD's server CPUs broadening, Micron's memory tightness and Intel's "jaw-dropping" target — as the story shifts from capex build to utilisation and monetisation.
